jobs.description:
Job Description

Helping others improve and turn their lives around – there’s no better feeling. It’s what we do for thousands of people at more than 150 sites across the UK. Be a part of it.

We are looking for an outstanding Kitchen Assistant/Catering Assistant who’s passionate about food and wants to make a difference. 

You’ll be working Part time 10 hours a week at Cygnet Hospital Bierley, creating an excellent experience for the people in our care. 

Cygnet Hospital Bierley provides a range of acute and low secure mental health services for men and women.

The hospital is set across four wards offering single-sex male and female specialist mental health services. All our services are provided under the umbrella of a recovery orientated approach and are reviewed through the CPA framework.

Cygnet Hospital Bierley has a true focus on the service user and the over-riding aim of providing the best quality treatment and care possible. The team are committed to delivering care and treatment guided by the principles of a trauma informed approach.

• Strong career progression opportunities• Expert supervision & support• Pension scheme• Cycle to work scheme & employee discount savingPlease note: successful candidates will be required to undergo an enhanced DBS check.

What next?

If you care about making a difference – we want to talk to you.

jobs.title: Office Manager - Part Time
jobs.description:
Job Description

Office Manager (Part-Time)

Leeds – Morley | 3 Days Per Week (Office-Based) | £36,000 FTE


About the Opportunity

Our client is a successful and growing technology business based in the heart of Leeds. With a strong reputation in its sector and an ambitious growth strategy, they are seeking a highly organised and proactive Office Operations Manager to play a key role in supporting the day-to-day running of the business.


This is a varied and rewarding position that combines office management, finance administration, HR support, supplier management and compliance responsibilities . Working closely with the leadership team, you will become a central figure in ensuring operational efficiency across the organisation.


The Role

This opportunity is ideal for someone who enjoys bringing structure, improving processes and taking ownership of business administration. You'll be responsible for keeping essential operational functions running smoothly while supporting colleagues across multiple departments.


Key Responsibilities


Office & Facilities Management

  • Oversee office suppliers, facilities and workplace services
  • Coordinate maintenance, repairs and office improvements
  • Manage office equipment and supplies
  • Liaise with landlords, contractors and service providers
  • Organise team events and employee engagement activities
  • Ensure a professional, productive and well-maintained office environment
  • Maintain Health & Safety records and documentation
  • Coordinate workplace compliance requirements
  • Manage Right to Work records and documentation
  • Ensure company records remain accurate and up to date
  • Handle confidential employee and business information appropriately


Finance & Business Administration

  • Process supplier invoices and maintain accurate financial records
  • Support purchase and sales ledger activities
  • Manage employee expense processing
  • Assist with payroll administration
  • Maintain supplier and customer databases
  • Support month-end financial processes and reporting
  • Manage contract and renewal schedules
  • Produce operational and cost reports for management


Supplier & Cost Management

  • Monitor company overheads and operational expenditure
  • Manage software subscriptions, licences and supplier contracts
  • Track contract renewals and key supplier relationships
  • Identify cost-saving opportunities and efficiencies
  • Obtain quotations and support supplier negotiations
  • Ensure supplier invoices align with agreed terms
  • Assist with budget monitoring and expenditure controls


HR Administration

  • Maintain employee records and HR documentation
  • Coordinate recruitment administration and interview scheduling
  • Support onboarding and offboarding processes
  • Monitor absence, holiday and sickness records
  • Coordinate probation reviews and appraisal processes
  • Maintain HR policies and employee handbook documentation
  • Support employee relations and performance management administration
  • Ensure HR compliance with current employment legislation


Essential Experience & Skills

  • Previous experience in working as an office manager
  • Strong finance administration, bookkeeping or accounting support experience
  • Excellent organisational and prioritisation skills
  • Knowledge of Xero or similar accounting software
  • High attention to detail and accuracy
  • Experience managing suppliers, contracts and operational budgets
  • Strong IT skills, including spreadsheets and business systems
  • Excellent communication and interpersonal skills
  • Ability to take ownership and work proactively


What's on Offer?

  • Flexible part-time working arrangement
  • Broad and varied role with genuine responsibility
  • Opportunity to work closely with senior leadership
  • Friendly, collaborative and supportive culture
  • Chance to make a tangible impact within a growing business
  • Central Leeds location with excellent transport links


If you're someone who thrives on organisation, enjoys improving processes and wants to make a meaningful contribution to a growing business, we'd love to hear from you.


Due to the amount of response we receive, unfortunately we are not able to give feedback to individuals, if you have not heard back within 5 days please assume that you have not been successful for the role you have applied for. By applying to this advertisement, you are hereby giving consent for Jo Holdsworth Recruitment to hold your details for a 30 day period and contact you via any method of contact you have listed on your application.

Work Location: In person

jobs.title: Business Development Lead - NHS & Public Sector | Remote | Full-time or Part-time (minimum 3 days...
jobs.description:
Job Description

About the Role


We’re looking for someone to help us turn proven Strengthify work into new organisational opportunities across the NHS, Higher Education and wider public sector.


This is a new business role, but not a high-volume or transactional sales role.


At Strengthify, we help leaders, managers and teams strengthen how they work together in real organisational environments - particularly during pressure and change.


Our work combines practical strengths-based development, facilitated workshops and programmes, and Strengthify Engage - our digital platform designed to help new ways of working become visible, usable and embedded over time.


We’re now looking for someone who can help us take what is already working and bring it to more organisations, regions, services and decision-makers.


That might mean identifying where successful NHS work with postgraduate trainees, SAS doctors, LED doctors or leadership cohorts could be relevant elsewhere. It might mean helping universities understand how Strengthify can support teams through transformation, restructure or change. It might mean finding the right person in an organisation and starting a conversation that leads to meaningful work.


You’ll need to be comfortable creating opportunities, running credible early conversations with senior stakeholders, shaping next steps, and closing first pieces of business.


Just as importantly, we’re looking for someone who can judge which opportunities are worth pursuing. In some cases, the first step may be a paid pilot or focused initial project, but the goal is to build relationships that can grow within the first year and develop into recurring programmes, wider Engage adoption or longer-term organisational partnerships.


This is about good business, not just any business - pursuing work where Strengthify can create meaningful impact and where there is a credible path beyond the first engagement.


You won’t be doing this alone. You’ll work closely with our consultants, Relationship Manager, marketing team and founder. But we do want someone who can confidently open and progress conversations independently, before bringing others in at the right point.


This role is about impact as well as growth.


We want to grow because we believe Strengthify can help more organisations improve leadership, teamwork, collaboration and confidence in the places where those things matter most.


Who We Are


Strengthify helps leadership and teamwork hold up under pressure.


We support leaders responsible for departments, directorates and services to build more consistent leadership and teamwork across teams - so conversations, collaboration and coordination hold up through pressure and change.


Our approach brings together:


  • Strengthify Profile - a practical strengths and working styles framework
  • Facilitated development - workshops, programmes and team sessions
  • Strengthify Engage - the digital home of the Strengthify ecosystem, helping insight translate into everyday leadership and teamwork


We work mainly across:


  • NHS and health organisations
  • Higher Education
  • Local government and wider public services


We are still a small team, but we’re ambitious.


Longer term, we want Strengthify to become something organisations increasingly standardise around when they want to improve how managers, teams and leaders work together.


We’re not trying to sell isolated workshops. We’re building a connected ecosystem that helps development stick and supports better everyday work.


What You'll Do


You’ll help us create and close new organisational opportunities by taking proven work into new contexts.

This is likely to include:


  • Identifying where existing Strengthify work could be relevant to new organisations, regions or services
  • Building relationships with NHS, Higher Education and wider public sector decision-makers
  • Developing opportunities with medical education, workforce, OD, leadership, transformation and service leaders
  • Creating new conversations around areas such as postgraduate medical education, SAS and LED doctor development, leadership capability, team collaboration and organisational change
  • Running credible first meetings independently and identifying where Strengthify could add value
  • Prioritising opportunities with strong strategic fit, meaningful impact and a credible route to longer-term growth
  • Working with consultants and colleagues to shape relevant proposals and next steps
  • Converting qualified opportunities into first paid engagements
  • Supporting clean handover into relationship management once an organisation has entered the Strengthify ecosystem
  • Maintaining a clear and useful pipeline in HubSpot


Initially, we expect the role to be weighted towards NHS and health-related opportunities, while also developing relevant Higher Education and wider public sector work.


What We're Looking For


You might have worked in business development, consultative sales, partnerships, public sector growth, workforce development, leadership development, healthcare, Higher Education, consultancy or professional services.


What matters most is that you can build trust, understand organisational challenges, create opportunities and close meaningful business without becoming pushy or transactional.


We’re looking for someone who brings:


  • Proven experience creating, progressing and closing new business opportunities
  • Confidence running early-stage conversations with senior stakeholders
  • The ability to identify where a proven proposition could apply elsewhere
  • Strong relationship-building and communication skills
  • Commercial judgement and the ability to close deals appropriately
  • Curiosity about organisational challenges and public sector pressures
  • The confidence to work independently while collaborating closely with others
  • Strong written communication and proposal-shaping ability
  • A thoughtful, values-aligned approach to growth


Experience in or around the NHS would be particularly valuable. Experience in Higher Education or wider public sector environments would also be helpful.


The Practical Bits


  • Location: UK-based, remote working with occasional travel to meetings, events or workshops
  • Type: Full-time or part-time considered, with a minimum of approximately 3 days per week
  • Salary: £60,000 FTE base salary
  • OTE: Strong performers should be able to achieve £90,000-£120,000+ FTE, based on commission linked to new organisational business generated and won
  • Commission: Initially based on 10% of first-year revenue from new organisational business, subject to agreed terms. Commission is uncapped, but our emphasis is on building the right kind of business - relationships that create impact, trust and potential for long-term growth.
  • Holiday: 40 days per year FTE, including bank holidays
  • Pension: 5% employer contribution
  • Development: Ongoing professional development and support
  • Purpose: We help leaders, managers and teams strengthen how they work together in real organisational environments - particularly during pressure and change


We are open to different working patterns, provided there is enough availability to build momentum with prospects, follow up consistently and manage live opportunities well.


This may suit someone who wants a meaningful, commercially important role that fits alongside other commitments outside of work.


Why Join Strengthify?


This is a chance to help build something with real-world impact.


The work we do supports people who are leading teams, services and organisations through pressure, complexity and change.


When Strengthify works well, managers feel more confident, teams understand each other better, conversations improve, collaboration strengthens and organisations become better equipped to support their people.


We’re at an important stage.


We have strong foundations, meaningful proof points and a growing ecosystem. Now we need to turn that into more repeatable, sustainable and commercially successful growth.


You’ll have the opportunity to shape that next phase.

jobs.title: Finance Business Partner (part time)

jobs.title: Sales Development Representative - Self-Employed Conractor (Remote, full or part time)
jobs.description:
Job Description

Sales Development Representative — Self-Employed Contractor (Remote or Hybrid, Full or Part Time)


At FISCAL Technologies, we're not just selling software — we're partnering with finance leaders to protect over £350 billion of global spend every year through innovative AI-driven solutions that deliver ROI within three months.


We're looking for a passionate relationship builder who can open doors, book meetings and help develop sales opportunities — and who wants the flexibility and independence of working as a self-employed contractor rather than as a PAYE employee.


Important — please read before applying


This is a self-employed consultancy engagement, not an employed role. You'll invoice us on an agreed day rate, be responsible for your own tax and National Insurance (or local equivalent), and carry your own professional indemnity insurance. If you're looking for a salary, holiday pay, pension contributions or other employee benefits, this engagement isn't the right fit.


We have a strong preference for candidates based in the UK, US or Canada. For data security and information governance reasons, applications from candidates based and authorised to work in one of these three countries will be prioritised.


Successful candidates will be required to complete a basic background/security check, carried out in their country of residence, before being granted access to our internal systems. This is in line with our information security and data protection commitments to our customers.


The role


Working directly with our new business sales and marketing teams, your focus will be booking qualified new business meetings:


• Prospecting and lead generation — identifying and researching organisations that fit our ideal customer profile

• Outbound outreach — initiating contact through phone, email and social channels

• Lead qualification — assessing interest, budget and need against agreed criteria

• Booking meetings — scheduling qualified meetings and demonstrations for Account Executives

• Reporting and tracking outcomes

• Collaboration — working closely with sales and marketing colleagues on strategy and messaging


Required skills and experience


• Excellent verbal, written and listening communication

• Strong organisation and time management — comfortable managing a high volume of activity

• Proficiency with CRM systems and modern sales tools

• Persistence, self-motivation and the discipline that goes with self-employed working

• Prior SDR, BDR or outbound prospecting experience preferred


Commercial terms

• Day rate and weekly commitment to be agreed — we have flexibility on both

• Monthly invoicing, paid within 14 days of approved invoice

• Initial probation period with a short notice period, continuing by agreement thereafter

• Remote or hybrid (occasional visits to the office in Reading are possible with time and travel costs reimbursed)


Why FISCAL?


• Be part of an exciting growth company protecting organisations around the world

• Our solutions deliver meaningful impact for finance teams worldwide

• Flexibility and independence as a self-employed partner, not an employee

• Work alongside experienced sales and marketing colleagues backed by strong product-market fit


FISCAL Technologies is a previous recipient of the Queen's Award for Enterprise (Innovation) and is recognised as a great place to work. We're committed to working with a diverse network of contractors and partners that reflects the clients we serve.


To apply, please send a short message outlining your relevant experience, your location, and your indicative day rate and weekly availability.
